chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Why Briggs left Sissle after the 1930 Paris season
summary: Sissle returned to Paris in May 1930 and went back to the US in September, but Briggs refused the one-nighters and stayed in Europe.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, just to carry on with that for just a little bit, he was working with Mezzrow.
Yes, when he went back, he went back in 1940. No, 1930. When he went back to Sissle. When I left the orchestra, he went back with Sissle.
To Europe?
He went to America, with him, you see.
When I told him about this hard work, we did one-nighters, he said, "Well," he said, "Art, you don't work that hard in Europe." I said, "No, I realize, and I want to stay. (Laughter).
He said, "Well, I'm accustomed to it." So, he went back with Sissle.
Well, then, how did you get back to Europe?
Briggs
Huh?
How did you get back to Europe?
I came back with Sissle.
We came back together.
You mean Sissle came back here.
Oh, yes, we had contracts at the Ambassador.
Right.
But I did not go back with him. When he went back -- he went back and he went to the Park Central Hotel.
Right.
I wasn't with him then.
Okay. Well, let me get that straight. You came back -- when did Sissle come back to Paris?
Briggs
He came back in 1930.
At what time of the year.
He came back in 1930, because we opened at the Ambassador around about the 15th of May.
Right. So he came back then --
Yes.
Then, when did he go back to the States?
After that, at the end of that season, round about September.
I see, and then you left the band and stayed here.
I left, I told him I wouldn't go back.
Because of one-nighters?
Yes, I told him, it's too hard. He said he realized. I said, it was
Briggs
too hard, I said.
